summary: The complete uncommitted AS-M004 revision-2 delivery was reviewed in one fresh Codex context. The records and demonstration suites and the full CI-equivalent script pass. One mandatory resource-qualification defect remains: the purported process-tree RSS sampler follows only main-thread children, while the real capture fixture launches Git from the libtest worker thread. Live observation confirms those children are omitted systematically. Correct the sampler and renew the affected memory evidence; no additional production-code blocker was identified. This report does not accept or close the mission.

findings.title: Process-tree memory sampler omits children launched by the test thread
findings.issue: tree_rss walks /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children for each process. That is the leader thread's immediate-child list, not the union of children of all threads in the process. The libtest worker executes capture and launches the real Git children from a different TID. Their PIDs never enter this sampler's process list; rss_bytes therefore sums only the test/store process in the capture journeys.

causalReproduction.instrumentation: Ran this unchanged real fixture from a Python parent. While it ran, read /proc/<records_measure-pid>/task/*/children and each observed child's comm; compare with /proc/<records_measure-pid>/task/<records_measure-pid>/children. No source was edited.
causalReproduction.reproduce: Run the command with an external /proc observer; locate its records_measure process, enumerate every task's children, and compare the live Git child's parent TID with the PID used by line 57. The leader list is empty while the worker list contains Git. The kernel documentation specifies that children belongs to the particular PID/TID pair.

findings.impact: The mandatory capture/save resource observation does not account for the whole owned process tree. The retained text's claim that live Git children are included is false; this is more than the disclosed chance of missing short peaks at a 1 ms sampling interval. It does not prove a product budget overrun or a production storage defect, but the mission cannot be accepted with this required evidence incomplete.
findings.boundedCorrection: In the existing measurement harness, collect children across all /proc/<pid>/task/*/children entries for each owned process and recurse, deduplicating process PIDs, or use an already available external whole-process observer that covers thread-launched children. Verify against an actual live Git child during the real capture fixture, rerun the affected memory journeys, and retain corrected source-linked measurements and limits in new evidence without overwriting historical observations. Preserve the sampling/RSS limitations. No new production framework, CLI, workload or physical-fault certification is required.

contractAssessment.criterion: Synchronous capture retention and fresh-process reads after source loss
contractAssessment.detail: save_capture consumes real workspace::Capture without recapture or configuration re-resolution. Header, ordered change membership, source bytes/roles/generations/Git modes/blob identities and captured configuration commit in one SQLite transaction. The full retained JSON/range equality test deletes the repository and reads through a child process. Deletion, present empty bytes, legitimate empty selection and repeated occurrence identities remain distinct.

The records-owned domain-separated, length/presence-encoded SHA-256 covers header, membership, ordinals, provenance and bytes in both save and read. Reconstruction uses the same read snapshot and explicitly rejects inconsistent membership. Missing, extra/duplicate, altered source/configuration and provenance regressions pass. It is an integrity digest, not a MAC or a replacement workspace identity. Whole-capture deletion is NotFound; no new adversarial guarantees are inferred. AUTOINCREMENT occurrences are independent even for equal capture generations.

Only unshipped schema v1 exists. Initialization DDL and user_version are transactional; the conflicting-object test leaves version zero and no partial tables. Unchanged reopen, newer unsupported version, unrelated database, malformed file and unavailable parent are exercised. The existing schema check is limited to the store table names and integrity column; it is not a full schema fingerprint. Missing/incompatible columns subsequently produce explicit SQLite errors, not a clean captured result. No invented migration framework is needed.

contractAssessment.criterion: Complete-or-absent transactions and honest acknowledgement outcomes
contractAssessment.detail: BEGIN IMMEDIATE and one SQLite commit contain all bytes/references. Insert/trigger failure, lock-wait termination, actual WAL-write EIO and kill inside commit are exercised. The during-commit interposer stops before real WAL sync returns, after frames are written; reopening may legitimately find the attempt complete. A postcommit/preack kill leaves a readable record and does not imply absence. CommittedUnmeasured carries the committed id when measurement fails; committed over-limit usage is explicit and never deletes evidence. General I/O errors are not proof of absence. This is process/call-boundary evidence, not power-loss or device certification.

contractAssessment.criterion: 80% warning, quota admission, reservations and concurrent writers
contractAssessment.detail: Warning uses u128 integer arithmetic; refusal compares measured retained bytes plus a checked reservation against the explicit per-store budget. The write lock owns reservation lifetime, preventing two writers from simultaneously admitting against the same remaining capacity without a separate ledger. Refusal and recovery preserve retained reads. DB, WAL, SHM and journal lengths, overflow/page and b-tree allowances, checkpoint duplication and existing WAL backlog are included. Held-reader file/directory symlink regressions now use the effective canonical path; new/dangling symlink cases pass. The formula is conservative application policy, not physical disk reservation or a formal arbitrary-filesystem bound.

Page size is read at open; WAL and synchronous FULL are set and verified. The reviewed bundled build supplies default zero reserved bytes and default auto-checkpoint behavior. Actual workspace/config owners bound acquired inputs; the formula computes the actual retained row and byte lists rather than relying only on inventory file count. The fixed page/metadata allowances and 64 KiB auxiliary margin remain engineering assumptions falsified by near-boundary, metadata-heavy, large-write, backlog and checkpoint fixtures. Different SQLite builds/settings or unsupported path replacement need qualification; no hard-quota claim is accepted.

Capture-only and capture/save/read latency, separate open/reopen and synchronous-save cost, plus actual DB/auxiliary storage were reproduced. Existing 20/30-observation percentile and one-host warm-cache limits are explicit. Storage sampling is a lower bound. Whole-owned-process memory is not established because of the reproduced finding; the retained 'tree RSS' values must not be treated as complete tree measurements.

records is one cohesive module hiding SQLite schema, transactions, admission and reconstruction behind open/save/read/usage. Workspace/config enums and identities are reused; SQL and binding errors do not escape as provider-specific/public DB types. Stored owned rows and borrowed digest views localize one canonical integrity implementation; their duplication serves distinct lifetimes. Long linear save/read methods are cohesive rather than an automatic reason to add layers. No background queue, external blob protocol, universal AST/result type, new crate or speculative migration/plugin framework was added. No architecture blocker was identified in this single review context.

The actual delta is one exact rusqlite 0.41.1 dependency with default features disabled and bundled SQLite, plus nine locked additions without unrelated package upgrades. Installed rusqlite transaction/drop behavior and bundled build source were inspected. P01 policy evidence qualifies the selected graph; P01C1 records complete-graph qualification and locked Node restoration. The initial import-only RED and pre-age-check downloads remain historical deviations covered solely by the explicit process-exception-authority.txt; they are not relabelled compliant or used to waive later checks. Later corruption, admission and alias corrections retain actual behavioral RED evidence. No install, live registry requalification, version recommendation or provider change was performed here.

report: REQUEST CHANGES. One high-severity qualification defect remains: the process-tree memory observer reads only the leader-thread children file, while the actual Rust test worker launches Git from a different thread. The unchanged protocol passed, but an external observer saw Git PID 2116266 under TID 2106694 of test process 2106689 while the leader's child list was empty. Those children are therefore absent from the reported tree RSS regardless of sampling frequency. Correct the existing observer, verify it against real live Git children, and renew the affected memory evidence and claims. Preserve historical measurements and their applicability limits. The full contract was examined in one fresh review context, including source capture/save/read after source loss, integrity and occurrence distinctions, schema/version handling, complete-or-absent writes, postcommit truth, quota/refusal/concurrency, effective path aliases, resource evidence, dependency/process history, design ownership and the complete nonvisual demonstration. The 38 records tests, two demo tests, real resource fixture and complete CI-equivalent checks pass. No additional production-code or architectural blocker was found; these checks do not cure the reproduced mandatory measurement gap. The initial TDD/download deviations retain only their explicit historical exception. No specialist lanes or nested agents ran, and no source was repaired. This is the terminal independent review result for Firstmate to examine and register, not packet acceptance, mission closure or publication authority.
